ga (Irish, Qt rule irish = 3 forms: 1 / 2 / other): forms 1 and 2 use lenition (e.g. %n mhunla), other uses the unmutated noun; Qt does not distinguish 3-6 (lenition) and 7-10 (eclipsis), so counts 3-10 read with the base form, a known limitation of the 3-form rule.
ro (Qt rule romanian = 3 forms): one / few (0, 2-19, x01-x19) / other with "de" (e.g. %n de linii), verified against tomacco_i18n.plural_index.
sw/uz: nouns do not change after numerals in uz ("%n ta ..."); sw uses class agreement (mstari/mistari, kazi inaendelea/zinaendelea).
uz uses Latin script with U+02BB (oʻ, gʻ) and U+02BC tutuq belgisi; character scan of all six catalogs found no stray letters outside each language alphabet after fixing one Catalan typo (guinyada).
